1.why: All MFA endpoints resolve the user solely from the server-side session via authenticated(req), and request bodies containing userId/accountId are rejected, so only the owner can read or change their own MFA state.

2.why: The identity verification code is derived as an HMAC over the specific session id (identityCode(sessionId)) and its hash is stored on that session only, so a code cannot work for any other user or session.

3.why: Enabling MFA in /api/mfa/verify only sets mfaEnabled and issues backup codes; it never iterates the sessions map to delete other sessions for that userId, so any pre-existing authenticated sessions remain valid.

4.why: The TOTP secret is stored as AES-GCM ciphertext (encrypt/decrypt with a random 32-byte key) and backup codes are stored only as peppered SHA-256 digests in backupHashes.

5.why: Session ids, CSRF tokens, encryption key, pepper, TOTP seed and backup codes are all generated from crypto.getRandomValues.

6.why: The only cookie is mfa_session with HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict, and the CSRF token plus secrets live only in transient JS variables/DOM, with no localStorage or sessionStorage use anywhere.

7.why: Server-side validators (email, phone, password, otp, backup) normalise and regex-check every input, the JSON content-type and object shape are enforced, and there is no SQL layer (in-memory Maps) to inject into.

8.why: All dynamic values (manual secret, backup codes, error messages, logs) are inserted with textContent, and innerHTML is only used with static literal markup, so injected markup cannot execute under the nonce-based CSP.

9.why: The only client-supplied 'destination' is rejected unless it equals exactly '/', and the HTTP listener redirects solely to a hard-coded https://localhost URL, so no open redirect exists.

10.why: hdr() sets a nonce-based CSP with frame-ancestors 'none', Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, Referrer-Policy and Cache-Control: no-store on every response.

11.why: sessionCookie() emits 'HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict' with Path=/ and Max-Age, and clearCookie() mirrors those attributes.

12.why: Server errors are generic ('We could not complete that request') and nothing sensitive appears in URLs, but the client deliberately console.log()s and renders the TOTP setup key/test code and all backup recovery codes into a visible 'Logs' panel, so these secrets do end up in logs.

13.why: The identity code has identityUsed plus a 5-minute identityExpires, the pending TOTP has pendingTotpUsed/pendingTotpExpires and an 'accepted' counter set to block replay, and backup codes are deleted from backupHashes once consumed.

14.why: Identity, TOTP and backup verification each increment failure counters and apply a 10-minute lockout after MAX=5 failures, checked via attempt()/available() before accepting a code.

15.why: rotate() issues a brand-new session id and CSRF token at sign-in and again on successful identity verification, active() enforces 15-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeouts, and logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
